issues.title: [Performance] Optimize DeepSeek V4.1 indexer weights projection overlap
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR optimizes **DeepSeek V4.1 Indexer weights projection scheduling** by adjusting the synchronization point between the main and auxiliary NPU streams. Previously, the main stream waited for `weights_done` immediately after Query RoPE. This introduced unnecessary serialization: the independent FP32 input cast could not overlap with the auxiliary weights projection, and query quantization was also delayed. The optimization defers this synchronization to **after the FP32 cast but before the C2 Compressor GEMMs**, enabling better Vector/Cube overlap while avoiding potential Cube resource contention. #### Implementation The change introduces a bounded overlap window for active C2 Compressor paths: 1. **Conditional synchronization**: Defer `weights_done` only when the current layer is a KV source using C2 compression (`compress_ratio == 2`) and has cache tokens to process. C1 and other paths retain the original synchronization behavior. 2. **Overlap weights projection with FP32 cast**: Allow `hidden_states.float()` on the main stream to execute concurrently with weights projection on the auxiliary stream. 3. **Launch query quantization earlier**: Record `quantize_start` after the FP32 cast and enqueue query quantization on the auxiliary stream, following weights projection. 4. **Preserve synchronization before Compressor GEMMs**: Wait for `weights_done` before `compressor.wkv()` and `compressor.wgate()` to avoid potential Cube resource contention. 5. **Maintain Indexer readiness**: `select_projected()` waits for `quantize_done` when available, falling back to `weights_done` if quantization was skipped. #### Execution order **Baseline:** ```text Aux: Weights Projection -> weights_done -> WAIT -> Query Quantization Main: Query RoPE -> WAIT weights_done -> FP32 Cast -> quantize_start -> WKV/WGate ``` **Optimized:** ```text Aux: Weights Projection -> weights_done -> WAIT -> Query Quantization Main: Query RoPE -> FP32 Cast -> quantize_start -> WAIT weights_done -> WKV/WGate ``` The key improvements are: - **Weights Projection (Cube) overlaps with FP32 Cast (Vector).** - **Query Quantization (Vector) can overlap with Compressor GEMMs (Cube).** - Weights Projection and Compressor GEMMs remain separated to avoid potential Cube contention. `quantize_start` is recorded before the main stream waits for `weights_done`, preventing circular dependencies between the streams. An earlier implementation deferred synchronization until Indexer TopK, but this caused a serving performance regression, potentially due to competing Cube workloads. The final implementation uses a shorter, controlled overlap window. #### Profiling observations The NPU timeline confirms the expected cross-stream scheduling changes. **Baseline:** In the baseline, the main stream waits for `weights_done` immediately after Query RoPE, delaying the FP32 Cast and subsequent query quantization. **Optimized:** After optimization: - **Main stream:** The FP32 Cast is moved before `EVENT WAIT`, allowing it to overlap with the auxiliary weights projection. - **Auxiliary stream:** The `EVENT WAIT` before query quantization is significantly shortened, allowing quantization to start earlier. - **Compressor GEMMs:** The main-stream synchronization is preserved before WKV/WGate to avoid potential Cube resource contention. This confirms that the optimization reduces unnecessary stream serialization while maintaining the required execution dependencies. ### Performance The final implementation was evaluated using alternating Baseline/PR runs in **A → B → A → B** order. Each run completed 200/200 requests with identical token counts, a configured request rate of 0.4 RPS, and identical speculative-decoding acceptance (60%, acceptance length 4). Results below are the arithmetic mean of two runs per configuration. | Metric | Baseline avg | PR avg | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | Output throughput (tok/s) | 214.545 | 214.620 | +0.03% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 2276.905 | 2157.165 | **-5.26%** | | P50 TTFT (ms) | 1742.715 | 1708.870 | **-1.94%** | | P95 TTFT (ms) | 5008.120 | 4130.180 | **-17.53%** | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 28.265 | 27.480 | **-2.78%** | | P50 TPOT (ms) | 26.460 | 25.695 | **-2.89%** | | P95 TPOT (ms) | 45.315 | 43.520 | **-3.96%** | | Mean E2EL (ms) | 17794.490 | 17242.085 | **-3.10%** | | P50 E2EL (ms) | 16368.390 | 16001.450 | **-2.24%** | | P95 E2EL (ms) | 27318.815 | 26360.785 | **-3.51%** | | P99 E2EL (ms) | 28819.315 | 27577.045 | **-4.31%** | The optimization improves latency while maintaining effectively unchanged throughput, as the workload is request-rate limited.
Benchmark configuration - Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 W4A8 - Parallelism: DP1, TP4, PCP2, expert parallel enabled - Scheduler: `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`, `max_num_seqs=16` - Cache/model length: block size 128, maximum model length 262144 - Graph mode: `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, extended NPU graph enabled - Indexer KV dtype: INT8 - DSV4 DSA multistream overlap enabled - DSpark speculative decoding: 5 draft tokens, synthetic acceptance length 4 - Workload: `prefix_repetition`, 200 prompts, 0.4 RPS, 45k shared prefix + 5k suffix + 550 output tokens ```bash vllm bench serve \ --backend openai-chat \ --model /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro \ --served-model-name illm \ --tokenizer /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro \ --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,e2el \ --metric-percentiles 50,95,99 \ --dataset-name prefix_repetition \ --request-rate 0.4 \ --num-prompts 200 \ --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --base-url http:// \ --ignore-eos \ --temperature 1 \ --seed 10801 \ --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 45000 \ --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 5000 \ --prefix-repetition-output-len 550 \ --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 1 \ --extra-body '{"cache_salt":"run-001"}' ```
### Does this PR introduce any user-facing changes? No. This optimization only adjusts internal cross-stream scheduling. It does not change APIs, configuration, defaults, or numerical behavior. ### How was this patch tested? **Regression tests** - Verified immediate vs. deferred weights synchronization. - Verified C2 execution order: FP32 Cast → query quantization enqueue → weights wait → Compressor WKV. - Verified C1 preserves its original synchronization behavior. - Verified `select_projected()` prioritizes `quantize_done` and falls back to `weights_done`. **Performance validation** - Compared Baseline and PR NPU timelines to inspect synchronization placement and overlap behavior. - Completed A/B/A/B Ascend serving benchmarks with graph capture/replay enabled. - All 800 requests completed successfully. **Static checks** - `python -m compileall -q vllm_ascend/attention/dsa_v41.py tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v41.py` - AST parsing - 120-character line-length check - `git diff --check` - Formatting, mypy, and unit checks are covered by GitHub CI. --- ### Checklist #### Testing - [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: C1, C2, skipped/deferred synchronization, and both readiness-event paths. - [x] **Regression test**: Event-order regression coverage in `tests/ut/attention/test_dsa_v41.py`. - [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: Not applicable to this scheduling-only change. - [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Assertions verify the synchronization event and its placement relative to Compressor GEMMs. - [x] **Performance impact**: A/B serving benchmark results and NPU Timeline comparison. vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542

issues.title: [Performance][Model] Fuse DeepSeek V4.1 SWA KV cache preparation
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 currently prepares SWA KV with three consecutive operators after the WKV projection: RMSNorm, interleaved partial RoPE, and paged-cache scatter. This PR replaces that chain with one A2 (910B) Triton kernel that consumes the raw BF16 WKV output and writes the normalized/rotated rows directly to their physical SWA cache coordinates.

The fused kernel:

- accumulates RMSNorm in FP32 and preserves the BF16 rounding boundary before RoPE;
- implements the existing adjacent-pair interleaved partial RoPE convention;
- uses the cache tensor's real block/row/feature strides;
- skips negative [block, offset] coordinates used by invalid slots and graph padding;
- launches on the caller's current stream, preserving the existing overlap between the KV branch and Wq_b GEMM;
- retains the original three-operator path for unsupported inputs.

Selection is limited to Triton-enabled A2 (910B), BF16 NPU WKV/cache tensors, DeepSeek V4.1's 512-wide standard SWA cache, compatible 2-D slot mappings, RMSNorm without a loaded bias, and at most 8192 rows. A3, A5 packed caches, unsupported layouts/dtypes, larger batches, Long KV, C1/C2 compressor, and indexer cache writes remain unchanged.

The fused path reduces the SWA preparation region from three kernels to one while avoiding the normalized KV intermediate and its subsequent RoPE/scatter global-memory traffic. WKV GEMM is intentionally left separate.

### Performance

The implementation was evaluated using alternating Baseline/PR runs in **A → B → A → B** order.

Each run completed 200/200 requests with identical token counts and identical speculative-decoding acceptance (60%, acceptance length 4).

Per-run results:

| Metric | A1 baseline | B1 PR | A2 baseline | B2 PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 1966.22 | 1881.39 | 1981.27 | 1874.66 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 28.15 | 25.86 | 26.21 | 25.99 |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 111.91 | 103.11 | 104.72 | 104.92 |
| Mean E2EL (ms) | 17420.41 | 16078.87 | 16369.37 | 16142.01 |

Results below are the arithmetic mean of two runs per configuration.

| Metric | Baseline avg | PR avg | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 214.525 | 214.680 | +0.07% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 1973.745 | 1878.025 | **-4.85%** |
| P50 TTFT (ms) | 1642.530 | 1568.960 | **-4.48%** |
| P95 TTFT (ms) | 2930.720 | 2838.645 | **-3.14%** |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 27.180 | 25.925 | **-4.62%** |
| P50 TPOT (ms) | 25.770 | 24.110 | **-6.44%** |
| Mean ITL (ms) | 108.315 | 104.015 | **-3.97%** |
| P50 ITL (ms) | 69.590 | 67.595 | **-2.87%** |
| P95 ITL (ms) | 500.810 | 480.680 | **-4.02%** |
| P99 ITL (ms) | 651.880 | 622.910 | **-4.44%** |
| Mean E2EL (ms) | 16894.890 | 16110.440 | **-4.64%** |
| P50 E2EL (ms) | 16039.690 | 15023.045 | **-6.34%** |
| P99 E2EL (ms) | 26434.795 | 26407.510 | **-0.10%** |

The optimization improves TTFT, TPOT, ITL, and end-to-end latency while maintaining output throughput. The largest improvements are **6.44% lower P50 TPOT** and **6.34% lower P50 E2EL**.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark configuration</summary>

- Hardware: Ascend 910B (A2)
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 W4A8
- Parallelism: DP1, TP4, PCP2, expert parallel enabled
- Scheduler: max_num_batched_tokens=4096, max_num_seqs=16
- Cache/model length: block size 128, maximum model length 262144
- Graph mode: FULL_DECODE_ONLY, extended NPU graph enabled
- Indexer KV dtype: INT8
- DSV4 DSA multistream overlap enabled
- DSpark speculative decoding: 5 draft tokens, synthetic acceptance length 4
- Workload: prefix_repetition, 200 prompts, 0.4 RPS, 45k shared prefix + 5k suffix + 550 output tokens

```bash
vllm bench serve \
  --backend openai-chat \
  --model /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro \
  --served-model-name illm \
  --tokenizer /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,95,99 \
  --dataset-name prefix_repetition \
  --request-rate 0.4 \
  --num-prompts 200 \
  --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \
  --base-url http://<server> \
  --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 1 \
  --seed 10801 \
  --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 45000 \
  --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 5000 \
  --prefix-repetition-output-len 550 \
  --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 1 \
  --extra-body '{"cache_salt":"run-001"}'
```

</details>

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Eligible DeepSeek V4.1 workloads on A2 (910B) automatically use the fused SWA cache-write path. There is no new API, parameter, configuration option, or environment variable.

### How was this patch tested?

**Regression and correctness coverage**

- Added CPU-routable coverage confirming that the fused branch consumes raw WKV output and bypasses standalone RMSNorm, RoPE, and scatter.
- Added hardware-profile coverage confirming A2 (910B) enables the fusion while A3 retains the baseline path.
- Added NPU coverage for 1 through 8192 rows, BF16 normalization rounding, interleaved partial RoPE, shuffled/negative slots, padded projection/RoPE/cache strides, untouched cache rows, and ACLGraph replay after input and slot updates.
- A3 and other unsupported hardware, dtype, shape, packed-cache, and large-batch cases retain the baseline path.

**Performance validation**

- Completed A/B/A/B Ascend serving benchmarks with graph capture/replay and DSV4 DSA multistream overlap enabled.
- All 800 requests completed successfully.
- Compared latency and throughput using the same model, serving configuration, seed, token counts, and speculative-decoding acceptance.

**Static and CPU checks**

- Python syntax compilation for all changed Python files.
- git diff --check.
- GitHub pre-commit, Ruff, mypy on Python 3.10/3.11/3.12, and CPU UT against both tested vLLM revisions passed:
  https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/42618075415
- All three commits are signed off.

Focused NPU commands:

```bash
pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/test_dsv41_swa_cache_fusion.py
python benchmarks/dsv41_swa_cache.py --tokens 1 8 32 128 512 2048 8192
```

The ready-precise/full NPU suite and profiler confirmation of auxiliary-stream overlap can be completed during PR review.

---

### Checklist

#### Testing

- [x] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: One-token decode, batches through the 8192-row fusion limit, negative slots, graph padding, non-contiguous physical strides, and graph replay.
- [ ] **Regression test**: This is a performance optimization rather than a correctness bug fix.
- [x] **Error / failure path coverage**: Unsupported hardware, dtype, shape, bias, packed-cache, and large-batch cases retain the baseline path.
- [x] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: Tests compare cache contents against an independent PyTorch reference and verify untouched rows.
- [x] **Performance impact**: A reproducible microbenchmark and an end-to-end A/B/A/B serving comparison are included.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58

issues.title: [Performance][DSV4.1] Use single-token decoder replay for DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill
issues.body:
## Summary

Adapt the prefill decoder replay optimization from [[vllm-project/vllm#62817](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62817)] to Ascend.

Replay only the last token for prefill chunks sufficiently far from the prompt end, reducing decoder computation while preserving the replay window needed by later chunks.

## Progress

- [x] Basic implementation
- [x] TP8 performance evaluation
- [x] PCP and SP support
- [ ] TP4 + PCP2 + SP correctness and performance evaluation

## Performance

Environment: 8 × Ascend 910B, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash W4A8.

**Both the baseline and optimized runs include the fix from [#20264](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/20264).** The baseline uses the existing 128-row bounded replay policy; the optimized version additionally enables this PR's single-row replay optimization. 

| Average cache hit rate | Baseline output throughput (tok/s) | Optimized output throughput (tok/s) | Throughput change | Baseline mean TTFT (ms) | Optimized mean TTFT (ms) | TTFT change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 30% | 110.87 | 113.24 | +2.14% | 238083.17 | 230404.09 | -3.23% |
| 50% | 143.13 | 145.16 | +1.42% | 117994.41 | 115533.82 | -2.09% |
| 90% | 217.37 | 217.38 | ≈0% | 1537.08 | 1558.81 | +1.41% |

### Benchmark command

```bash
AVG_HIT=30  # options 30/50/90
NUM_PROMPTS=200
NUM_PREFIXES=10
INPUT_LEN=50000
PREFIX_LEN=$((INPUT_LEN * AVG_HIT * NUM_PROMPTS / (100 * (NUM_PROMPTS - NUM_PREFIXES))))
SUFFIX_LEN=$((INPUT_LEN - PREFIX_LEN))
vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat 
--model /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro 
--served-model-name illm 
--tokenizer /data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-w4a8-chiro 
--percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el 
--metric-percentiles 50,95,99 
--dataset-name prefix_repetition 
--disable-shuffle 
--request-rate 0.4 
--num-prompts "$NUM_PROMPTS" 
--endpoint /v1/chat/completions 
--host 127.0.0.1 
--port 8080 
--ignore-eos 
--temperature 1 
--seed 10801 
--prefix-repetition-prefix-len "$PREFIX_LEN" 
--prefix-repetition-suffix-len "$SUFFIX_LEN" 
--prefix-repetition-output-len 550 
--prefix-repetition-num-prefixes "$NUM_PREFIXES" 
--ready-check-timeout-sec 0 
--extra-body "{\"cache_salt\":\"mixed-${AVG_HIT}-$(date +%s%N)\"}"
```

issues.title: [Performance] Fuse DeepSeek V4.1 indexer K cache writes and C2 RMSNorm
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

DeepSeek V4.1 currently publishes indexer K through separate RMSNorm, partial RoPE, dynamic INT8 quantization, and K/scale cache scatter operations. Its ratio-2 compressor also normalizes pooled output in a separate operation. These intermediate operations add kernel launches and global-memory traffic to the compressed-source path.

This PR introduces two Triton epilogue fusions:

- **Indexer K publication:** fuse RMSNorm, interleaved partial RoPE, per-token INT8 quantization, and direct writes to the paged K and FP16 scale caches. The `wk` projection remains a separate GEMM.
- **C2 pooling:** optionally apply RMSNorm inside the token-aligned pooling kernel, preserving the BF16 pooling-output boundary before normalization. FP32 ring-state updates retain their existing ordering.

The indexer kernel preserves the BF16 boundary between RMSNorm and RoPE, quantizes using an FP32 scale, and stores the dequantization scale in FP16. It respects physical cache strides and skips invalid physical slots. Valid output slots must remain unique.

The fused indexer path targets ordinary A2/A3 INT8 caches. A5 packed/folded cache publication and indexer Norm with a loaded bias retain the existing path. The C2 compressor also retains separate normalization when its Norm has a loaded bias, so that the bias is applied.

The intended benefit is fewer launches and intermediate memory accesses. 

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. This changes execution of DeepSeek V4.1 compressed-source processing, with the aim of reducing overhead. No new public API, command-line option, or environment variable is introduced.

### How was this patch tested?

Workload: approximately 50k input tokens and 550 output tokens per request; 200 successful requests, 0 failures, and 110,000 generated tokens in each reported run. Observed peak concurrency was 14 in both groups. The results below represent the mean values ​​obtained from two experimental repetitions conducted both before and after optimization.

| Metric | Baseline | Optimized | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Benchmark duration (s) | 507.78 | 507.79 | approximately unchanged |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 216.64 | 216.63 | approximately unchanged |
| TTFT mean (ms) | 1,536.41 | 1,525.35 | -0.72% |
| TPOT mean (ms) | 14.92 | 14.71 | -1.41% |
| ITL mean (ms) | 59.57 | 58.44 | -1.90% |

Speculative-decoding aggregate statistics were unchanged: reported acceptance rate 60.00%, acceptance length 4.00, 27,600 drafts, 138,000 draft tokens, and 82,800 accepted tokens.

#### Testing

- [ ] Boundary / edge-case tests added; NPU execution remains pending.
- [ ] Regression test added for loaded compressor Norm bias.
- [ ] Host-side shape, dtype, stride, epsilon, and device error paths covered.
- [ ] Native NPU numerical tests pass on the target stack.
- [ ] Preliminary author-provided profiling and serving summaries recorded, including the TTFT P99 increase.
- [ ] Raw measurements, environment details, and repeatability validation attached.
- [ ] Required repository checks and CI pass.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/24420b7a341af37a9bc3186e6fc6062512e0aa58
